learner_notice: Commit one response before feedback appears. Omission is available and is not scored as a selected misconception.

items.title: Starting check: relative deprivation
items.prompt: Residents' conditions improve slightly, but nearby communities improve much faster, increasing residents' sense of unfairness. Which mechanism is most direct?
options: Relative deprivation from a widening perceived comparison gap
Absolute deprivation because conditions reached the lowest possible level
Urban renewal because public buildings were replaced
Globalization because all local boundaries disappeared
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Guided practice: organization
items.prompt: A shared grievance persists for years, but collective action begins only after neighborhood groups build communication networks and assign coordinators. What changed?
options: The grievance appeared for the first time
Organizational capacity for sustained collective action
A specific tactic became the movement's entire purpose
Absolute resources became equal across all neighborhoods
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Less help: strategy versus tactic
items.prompt: A movement adopts a multi-year plan to change hiring rules and holds a one-day march within that plan. Which classification is correct?
options: Both are tactics because they involve collective action
The march is strategy and the multi-year plan is a tactic
The multi-year plan is strategy and the march is a tactic
Neither can be classified without measuring absolute deprivation
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: On your own: identify a tactic
items.prompt: Which example is best classified as a tactic rather than a broad movement strategy?
options: Pursue long-term change in national labor standards
Build a durable coalition across several industries
Shift public interpretation of workplace fairness
Coordinate a single petition delivery on a chosen date
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Near exit: explain emergence
items.prompt: A population perceives a widening unfair gap, develops shared language for the grievance, and forms funded local chapters. What best explains movement emergence?
options: Relative deprivation combined with growing organizational capacity
Absolute hardship alone automatically creates coordinated action
One isolated tactic explains the entire movement structure
A city-specific policy history is required before any explanation
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Changed exit: hold grievance constant
items.prompt: Two communities report the same relative deprivation. Only one develops sustained action after gaining leaders, meeting spaces, and communication tools. Which factor explains the difference?
options: The active community must have greater relative deprivation
The active community has greater organizational capacity
The inactive community selected the wrong urban-growth model
Both communities must use identical tactics at all times
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Repair the emergence chain
items.prompt: A neighborhood reports a widening fairness gap and also builds trained teams, meeting hubs, and communication lists. Which two-link explanation should be tested?
options: One tactic alone creates both the grievance and the entire organization
Absolute hardship automatically produces coordinated action without resources
Relative deprivation supplies motivation while organization supplies coordination
Urban renewal supplies motivation while globalization supplies all coordination
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: workplace mobilization
items.prompt: Workers compare stagnant wages with nearby gains, adopt a shared injustice frame, and create dues-funded committees across workplaces. What best explains movement emergence?
options: Absolute hardship alone, because organization is irrelevant
A single protest tactic, because grievances and resources are interchangeable
Urban decline combined with suburbanization
Relative deprivation combined with organizational capacity
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Repair causal isolation
items.prompt: If two cases have equal grievance but different mobilization, what should be compared next?
options: Their networks, leadership, roles, and usable resources
Whether both communities repeat exactly the same public slogan
Only their absolute income rankings within each community
The total number of urban buildings located in each case
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Fresh changed re-entry: resource loss
items.prompt: A movement's grievance and goal remain stable, but participation falls after communication channels and meeting sites are lost. What best explains the decline?
options: Relative deprivation necessarily disappeared
Reduced organizational capacity weakened mobilization
Global economic interdependence ended locally
The strategy became identical to one tactic
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Starting check: communication link
items.prompt: A low-cost messaging platform lets organizations on several continents coordinate in real time. Which globalization factor is most direct?
options: Relative deprivation produced by neighborhood comparison gaps
Urban decline produced by long-term central-city disinvestment
Communication technology reducing coordination across distance
Suburbanization produced by residential movement toward city outskirts
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Guided practice: interdependence
items.prompt: A component shortage in one country halts assembly in another and retail supply in a third. What does this illustrate?
options: Independent local economies with no shared production exposure
Gentrification driven by rising rents and higher-income in-migration
A social movement tactic directed only at local city government
Economic interdependence through a cross-border production chain
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Less help: compare perspectives
items.prompt: One analysis emphasizes wider market access; another emphasizes unequal bargaining power in the same global supply chain. How should they be read?
options: They foreground different distributed effects of one connection
Only the second can use evidence from economic networks
Only the first can describe any globalization process
They prove communication technology has no social role
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: On your own: cultural hybridization
items.prompt: A local music scene adopts a global style but combines it with local language and instruments. Which social change is best represented?
options: Complete cultural isolation despite ongoing cross-border exchange
Hybridization through global diffusion and local adaptation
Urban decline produced only by long-term central population loss
Uniform replacement of every local language and cultural form
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Near exit: distinguish linked processes
items.prompt: Online collaboration spreads a design rapidly, while production is divided across several countries. Which explanation is most complete?
options: The case contains no social or economic connection across distance
Only local urban renewal can explain both cross-distance changes
Communication technology and economic interdependence operate together
One movement tactic determines the entire communication and production network
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Changed exit: locate the transmitting link
items.prompt: A port closure delays medicine production abroad despite uninterrupted internet communication. Which mechanism transmits the main disruption?
options: Cultural hybridization through globally shared media content
Suburbanization around the port through outward residential movement
Relative deprivation within a locally organized social movement
Economic interdependence through material supply links
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Repair globalization tracing
items.prompt: What should a globalization explanation identify before naming an effect?
options: The cross-distance connection and what flows through it
A policy recommendation for every connected country
A complete geopolitical history of all locations
Whether every local culture becomes identical
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: transnational care network
items.prompt: Families in several countries use video calls and shared transfers to coordinate caregiving. Which interpretation is strongest?
options: Urban decline eliminates every form of long-distance family interaction
Communication and economic links support a transnational social network
The families become culturally identical after one video call
A single neighborhood tactic explains all of the cross-border ties
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Repair transmission-path isolation
items.prompt: If digital communication continues but a physical input cannot cross borders, which link should be examined?
options: Only the language used in online messages
Whether local music becomes culturally hybrid
The material supply chain connecting production sites
Whether a social movement changes its slogan
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Fresh changed re-entry: financial shock
items.prompt: A lending contraction in one region reduces investment by firms in several connected countries. Which explanation fits best?
options: Cultural diffusion makes all firms use identical symbols
Urban renewal directly moves every firm to a suburb
Relative deprivation automatically creates a movement
Economic interdependence transmits a financial shock
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Starting check: urban growth
items.prompt: Manufacturing jobs concentrate near a transport hub, and population grows around the hub. Which process is most direct?
options: Industrialization contributing to urban growth
Suburbanization away from an urban core
Gentrification through higher-income in-migration
Urban decline through central disinvestment
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Guided practice: suburbanization
items.prompt: Households and retail activity move from a central city toward surrounding residential areas. Which process is described?
options: Urbanization from rural areas into a growing central-city core population
Suburbanization through outward residential and activity movement
Gentrification within a lower-income central neighborhood after reinvestment
Globalization through a cross-border production, trade, and communication chain
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Less help: urban decline
items.prompt: A central district loses population and employers while buildings receive less investment. Which process best fits?
options: Urban growth
Suburban renewal
Urban decline
Cultural hybridization
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: On your own: planned redevelopment
items.prompt: A city funds rehabilitation of public buildings and utilities without evidence of higher-income in-migration. Which label is best supported?
options: Gentrification necessarily causing displacement
Suburbanization through household movement outward
Urban decline through loss of investment
Urban renewal through planned redevelopment
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Near exit: linked outward movement and decline
items.prompt: Population and businesses move toward suburbs while the central core loses tax base and investment. Which explanation is most complete?
options: Suburbanization occurs alongside urban decline
Gentrification occurs without any neighborhood investment
Urban growth occurs equally in every spatial zone
Global communication causes complete cultural uniformity
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Changed exit: distinguish gentrification
items.prompt: A lower-income neighborhood receives new investment, higher-income residents move in, rents rise, and displacement pressure increases. Which process is best supported?
options: Urban decline caused by withdrawal of all investment
Gentrification involving reinvestment and socioeconomic change
Suburbanization caused only by movement away from the core
Industrialization caused by new manufacturing employment
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Repair linked spatial change
items.prompt: Residents and firms move toward a metro edge while the old core loses revenue and maintenance. Which paired interpretation preserves both links?
options: Gentrification alongside rising central investment
Globalization alongside cultural uniformity
Suburbanization alongside urban decline
Urban renewal alongside equal growth in every zone
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: edgeward relocation
items.prompt: Over a decade, jobs and households relocate to outer municipalities while central vacancies rise and public investment contracts. Which linked change is best supported?
options: Gentrification coupled with rising core investment
Urban renewal coupled with stable central occupancy
Industrialization coupled with equal growth in all zones
Suburbanization coupled with urban decline
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Repair renewal–gentrification boundary
items.prompt: What additional evidence is needed to distinguish gentrification from redevelopment alone?
options: Higher-income in-migration with rising costs or displacement pressure
Whether the city publishes a formal redevelopment project schedule and budget
Whether any building receives a new coat of exterior paint during renewal
Whether the neighborhood lies entirely inside the city's municipal boundaries
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Fresh changed re-entry: renewal without replacement
items.prompt: Transit and parks are renovated, but resident income distribution, rents, and displacement remain stable. Which conclusion is strongest?
options: Gentrification is proven whenever any physical improvement occurs in the area
Urban renewal is supported, while gentrification is not established
Suburbanization is proven despite no outward resident or business movement
Urban decline is proven because public infrastructure spending increased
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.
